title: Unify policy engine for region/tier/fallback routing + schema validator
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The current routing policies for region selection, customer tier routing, and fallback model variants live in multiple evaluators across runtime and control-plane code. This has produced inconsistent behaviour (misordered fallbacks, region choices that ignore recent latency/capacity signals), brittle migrations when schema changes, and poor developer UX when users author policies (cryptic errors).

Goal: Refactor the policy engine to (1) provide a single canonical evaluator for routing rules that supports region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants; (2) introduce a DSL -> Intermediate Representation (IR) compilation step so policies can be validated and precompiled; (3) add a robust schema/semantic validator with actionable error messages and migration hints; (4) integrate the validator into the deployment/console flow and CI; (5) preserve runtime latency SLOs by precompiling and caching compiled policies.

Scope: This ticket covers the refactor of the core evaluator and the schema validator library used by the console and control plane. It does NOT include full policy migration tooling for customers (separate follow-up) but includes helpers and a best-effort migration path for built-in templates.
acceptance_criteria: Single evaluator library (policy-eval) that takes a compiled IR and returns deterministic routing decisions for a request context
DSL schema JSON Schema and semantic validator that surfaces clear errors and suggested fixes
Precompilation step added to CI that rejects invalid policies and prints migration hints
End-to-end tests covering region selection, tier routing logic, and fallback ordering including edge cases (no capacity, region down, model variant mismatch)
Benchmark: policy evaluation p50 < 500us and p99 < 2ms when using cached compiled IR on typical node types
Rollout gated behind feature flag with automatic fallback to legacy evaluator if failures detected
tasks: Spike: evaluate IR shapes and runtime API (done)
Design DSL grammar and JSON Schema (in progress)
Implement compiler from DSL -> IR (impl + unit tests)
Replace control-plane evaluator to use compiled IR (canary rollout)
Add schema validator to Console / CI with helpful error strings and links to docs
Add property-based tests and fuzzing for policy inputs
Add telemetry events for policy evaluation failures and fallbacks
Docs: update policy authoring guide and migration note
decisions: Use a small, typed IR instead of interpreting DSL at runtime to reduce eval latency and facilitate validation
Precompile policies in control-plane and ship compiled blobs to runtime agents; keep a bounded cache with TTL to allow live updates
Schema format: primary check via JSON Schema for surface/shape; supplement with semantic validator for rules that can't be expressed in JSON Schema (e.g., cyclic fallbacks, unreachable variants)
Feature-flag rollout rather than big-bang switch to allow quick rollback on customer-impacting issues
tradeoffs: Precompilation reduces runtime latency but adds complexity during deploys (need cache invalidation). We accept that cost to maintain p99 latency budgets.
IR restricts expressivity compared to full runtime scripting; we will cover advanced cases via 'custom route hooks' plugin surface in a follow-up ticket.
Relying on JSON Schema keeps validator simple for surface checks but requires additional semantic rules to capture routing invariants (added complexity in validator code)
progress_notes: 2026-02-24: Spike completed. Evaluated two IR approaches: node-based tree (preferred) vs tuple opcodes. Chosen tree-like IR for easier debugging and compactness.
2026-02-28: DSL design draft posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Policy+Engine+DSL (internal). Feedback from Priya Nair: favor explicit 'capacity_hint' field for region selectors.
2026-03-03: PoC compiler implemented in policy-eval/poc branch. Basic TTL cache and evaluation harness present. Initial microbenchmarks show p50 ~220us on c6gn-like instance.

2026-03-08: Security review triage: validator needs to ensure policies cannot reference internal-only model ids; added rule to semantic validator. PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3456

2026-03-10: Switched assignee to Diego Martinez to implement production compiler, testing harness, and CI integration. Working on JSON Schema and improved error messages for missing 'fallback' arrays.
